problem_text:
A logistics manager is assembling a fleet of cargo drones for a critical delivery mission spanning three distinct operational zones. The manager must select a combination of cargo modules to maximize total utility points while adhering to the total payload mass constraint.

The available cargo modules are:
* Module A: mass 50kg, utility 161 points
* Module B: mass 2kg, utility 102 points
* Module C: mass 18kg, utility 110 points
* Module D: mass 33kg, utility 290 points
* Module E: mass 46kg, utility 66 points
* Module F: mass 20kg, utility 235 points
* Module G: mass 12kg, utility 66 points
* Module H: mass 4kg, utility 243 points
* Module I: mass 34kg, utility 280 points
* Module J: mass 36kg, utility 298 points
* Module K: mass 35kg, utility 202 points
* Module L: mass 27kg, utility 172 points
* Module M: mass 39kg, utility 182 points
* Module N: mass 15kg, utility 179 points
* Module O: mass 32kg, utility 84 points
* Module P: mass 34kg, utility 23 points
* Module Q: mass 48kg, utility 256 points
* Module R: mass 9kg, utility 10 points
* Module S: mass 6kg, utility 297 points
* Module T: mass 2kg, utility 80 points
* Module U: mass 49kg, utility 66 points

Furthermore, due to compatibility protocols, exactly one of Module A and Module B must be included in the final configuration.

If Module C is selected, its specialized support systems impose a 10 kg reduction on the effective total payload capacity.
The aggregate payload mass for the drone fleet cannot exceed 385 kg. The manager must determine the optimal selection of modules.
